newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Leningrad region sees $100 mln loan, no eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Leningrad region sees $100 mln loan, no eurobond.

text.p: Russia's Leningrad region expects to get a three-year $100 million syndicated bank loan and has dropped plans to issue a Eurobond, the deputy governor of the region said on Wednesday.

"To do a rating is too much work -- we dropped the Eurobond idea when we understood that and decided to get a syndicated loan," Sergei Susekov told Reuters without giving details of when he expected to receive the credit.
Susekov said he expected leading German, French and Swiss banks to participate in a group of 12 or more banks extending the loan.
"There is no lead yet," he said, but added that Price Waterhouse was acting as an advisor for the loan.
He said he believed Leningrad region, surrounding St Petersburg in northern Russia, could pay 8-9 percent per year interest rates for the credit.
